name: Gallbladder
kicker: Small pouch under the liver · Stores bile and squeezes it out to digest fat
dates: Holds only a few tablespoons of bile
briefing: The gallbladder, a small, pear-shaped pouch tucked under the liver, stores and concentrates bile, a greenish fluid the liver makes all day long. When a fatty meal arrives, a hormone called CCK makes it squeeze bile into the small intestine, where bile breaks fat into tiny droplets. Sometimes bile hardens into gallstones, and doctors can remove the whole organ, because people can live without it.
answerHtml: Gallbladder (accept gall bladder; prompt on biliary system; do not accept “liver,” “pancreas,” or “bile duct”)

qb.tip: Search QBReader for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked) to see how real tossups clue it.

tossups.p: In 1882, the German surgeon Carl Langenbuch [“LAHNG-en-bookh”] performed the first successful operation to remove this organ, which is now one of the most common surgeries. People can live without this organ, because the liver can still send its fluid straight to the intestine.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this small, pear-shaped organ that stores bile made by the liver.

tossups.p: The hormone cholecystokinin [“koh-luh-sis-toh-KY-nin”], whose name means “bile sac mover,” is released by the duodenum when fatty food arrives and makes this organ contract. At the same time, the sphincter of Oddi [“ODD-ee”] relaxes so this organ’s contents can flow into the intestine.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this organ that stores bile and releases it to help digest fats.

tossups.p: Horses, deer, and rats all lack this organ, so bile flows straight from their livers into their intestines. In humans, this organ makes the bile it holds more concentrated by absorbing water from it between meals.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this small, pear-shaped organ tucked under the liver, where gallstones can form.

tossups.p: A medicine that can slowly dissolve some of the stones that form in this organ is named for bears, because its main chemical was first found in bear bile. Most of those stones are made largely of cholesterol, while others are dark “pigment” stones.
tossups.r: Those stones are called gallstones. For 10 points, name this organ that stores bile from the liver.

tossups.p: King Goujian [“GOH-jyen”] of Yue is said to have tasted the bitter fluid stored in this organ every day to remind himself of a defeat, a story behind a Chinese saying about perseverance. In Chinese, having a “big” one of these organs means being bold or brave.
tossups.r: The liver makes that fluid, called bile. For 10 points, name this organ beneath the liver that stores bile.

tossups.p: This organ is divided into a rounded fundus, a body, and a narrow neck, which leads into the cystic duct. The cystic duct joins the common hepatic duct from the liver to form the common bile duct.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this small organ that stores and concentrates bile, where gallstones can form.

tossups.p: Doctors check for Murphy’s sign, named for the surgeon John B. Murphy, by pressing below the right ribs as a patient breathes in, to see whether this organ is inflamed. Inflammation of this organ, often caused by a stone blocking its duct, is called cholecystitis [“koh-luh-sis-TY-tis”].
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this pear-shaped organ, which can be removed if gallstones form in it.

tossups.p: Ultrasound scans are usually the first test doctors use to look for stones in this organ, which show up as bright spots that cast dark “shadows” on the screen. Those stones can form when bile holds more cholesterol than it can dissolve.
tossups.r: Removing this organ is one of the most common surgeries. For 10 points, name this organ that stores bile, where gallstones form.

tossups.p: This organ releases a fluid whose salts emulsify fats, breaking large fat globules into tiny droplets that the enzyme lipase can digest more easily. That fluid, which this organ stores but does not make, contains no digestive enzymes of its own.
tossups.r: The liver makes that fluid. For 10 points, name this organ that stores bile until a fatty meal arrives.

tossups.p: A stone that slips out of this organ and blocks the common bile duct can cause jaundice, a yellowing of the skin and eyes from a buildup of bilirubin [“bil-ih-ROO-bin”]. This organ sits in the upper right part of the abdomen.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this small, pear-shaped organ that stores bile from the liver.

tossups.p: Starting in the late 1980s, surgeons began removing this organ through a few tiny cuts, using a camera on a thin tube, in a “laparoscopic” [“lap-uh-roh-SKOP-ik”] operation that soon became the usual method. The medical name for that operation is cholecystectomy [“koh-luh-sis-TEK-tuh-mee”].
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this organ that stores bile and can be removed if stones form in it.

tossups.p: The greenish-yellow color of the fluid stored in this organ comes from pigments such as bilirubin, which forms when old red blood cells are broken down. That fluid is made by the liver and reaches this organ through the cystic duct.
tossups.r: Hardened lumps called gallstones can form inside it. For 10 points, name this pouch under the liver that stores and concentrates bile.

tossups.p: Most stones in this organ never cause symptoms, but a stone that blocks its outlet can cause a sudden pain under the right ribs, called biliary colic, often after a fatty meal.
tossups.r: Those stones are called gallstones. For 10 points, name this organ that stores bile and squeezes it into the small intestine.

tossups.p: Fluid from this organ and juice from the pancreas enter the duodenum together through an opening called the ampulla of Vater [“FAH-ter”]. A stone from this organ that gets stuck there can inflame the pancreas.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this organ, which stores bile between meals and sits under the liver.

tossups.p: Between meals, this organ makes the fluid it stores several times stronger by pulling water out of it, so it needs to hold only a few tablespoons. A fatty meal makes this organ’s muscular walls squeeze.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this organ that receives bile from the liver through the cystic duct.

trap.title: Liver or gallbladder?
trap.body: The liver makes bile, but the gallbladder only stores and concentrates it, so a clue like “produces bile” wants the liver. The pancreas is a third neighbor whose duct meets the bile duct, and all three send juices into the duodenum. Gallstones themselves, or the bile duct a stone can block, are separate answers too.
trap.fix: “Makes” or “produces” bile means the liver. “Stores,” “concentrates,” or “squeezes out” bile, CCK making it contract, gallstones forming inside it, or a cholecystectomy means the gallbladder. Insulin or digestive enzymes mean the pancreas.
trap.line: Real answer line: Gallbladder (accept gall bladder; do not accept “liver” or “bile duct”)
